findings.finding: Per-window and per-segment anomaly scores were never persisted. stage_evaluate builds the grouped score table in memory and returns only aggregate AUCs.
findings.consequence: The six headline AUCs cannot be independently re-derived from any committed artifact without re-running model inference. Audit section 10 was not executable as specified.
findings.recommendation: Persist the per-segment score table (segment_id, labels, 7 score columns) alongside evaluate_*.json. This is a write of already-computed values and needs no re-scoring and no new test look.

findings.finding: No test asserts the number of Protocol-A test looks (exactly two, one per machine).
findings.consequence: A third undisclosed Protocol-A entry could be appended without failing the suite.
findings.recommendation: Assert exactly one Protocol-A look per machine and two in total.

findings.finding: 'differences are of the size expected from a nondeterministic training run' rests on a single run per machine, and the run was on CPU where the cited cuDNN nondeterminism does not apply.
findings.consequence: Overstates empirical support for an a-priori-plausible argument.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the weaker wording and attribute the gap to the execution environment difference rather than to nondeterminism within this run.

findings.finding: 'feature construction' in section 9 describes a pipeline Protocol A does not use.
findings.consequence: Implies the 98-feature Phase-3.1 representation was validated. It was not.

findings.finding: 'makes MechaSight's own results comparable to the literature' generalises a Protocol-A result to Protocol-B work.
findings.consequence: Overstates transfer across two pipelines that share almost nothing.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the claim to the Protocol-A path and the project's dataset handling.

findings.consequence: Weaker than the treatment given to every other artifact.

observations: The upstream validation split is window-level, so 1838 of 1839 RoboticArm segments appear in both training and validation. This is faithful to upstream and makes the validation loss optimistic, so early stopping is not clean model selection. Because of the best-state aliasing the only consequence for the reported metric is which epoch training stopped at.

The RoboticArm overlap is asymmetric: it touches the normal class only (212/232 normal test segments have a training sibling; 0/232 anomaly segments do). That asymmetry is precisely the structure that would produce optimistic bias, which strengthens the hedged claim without licensing a magnitude.
Every BrushlessMotor segment is its own parent (1593 parents for 1593 segments), so no sibling structure exists there and 0 crossing parents is structurally guaranteed, not incidental.
The string 'official_baseline_reproduction' names both a Phase-2 preprocessing profile and the Phase-3.3 ledger protocol value. No functional impact, but it is a collision when grepping.
The strict-tie AUC rule is immaterial on this data: reconstruction MSE scores are continuous, so exact ties are effectively impossible and the estimator coincides with sklearn.

claims.claim: the published IMAD-DS official baseline reproduces
claims.basis: all six comparisons NEAR_EXACT, worst 0.33 of a pre-frozen 0.5 band; tolerance committed 58 minutes before the first score and unchanged since

claims.claim: the differences are of the size expected from a nondeterministic training run
claims.basis: one run per machine, so no variance was measured; and the reproduction ran on CPU, where the cited cuDNN nondeterminism does not apply. The dominant driver of the gap is a different execution environment (device, backend, torch version) interacting with patience-3 stopping, not nondeterminism within this run
claims.action: reword to 'consistent with plausible run-to-run variation under the upstream nondeterministic implementation'

claims.claim: this makes MechaSight's own results comparable to the literature
claims.basis: what was validated is the Protocol-A path only. Protocol B uses different preprocessing, a different representation (98 engineered features), different models and a parent-disjoint split. None of that is exercised here
claims.action: narrow to: establishes a comparability anchor for Protocol-A-style numbers, and validates this project's dataset handling and official-split evaluation

claims.claim: recording overlap creates a credible mechanism for optimistic bias; the magnitude is to be measured
claims.basis: independently recomputed: 62/101 parents cross the split and the overlap is asymmetric - 212/232 normal test segments have a training sibling versus 0/232 anomaly. Correctly hedged; no magnitude asserted

claims.claim: Protocol A minus Protocol B is not a leakage estimate
claims.basis: scanned every Phase-3.3 artifact; no such arithmetic and no forbidden phrasing appears. The two protocols differ in split, preprocessing, representation and model family simultaneously

claims.claim: CPU use is authorised by upstream
claims.basis: the upstream notebook comment explicitly instructs adapting the device. That authorises the substitution but does not make it a bitwise-equivalent execution environment, and the report should not be read as claiming it does
claims.action: keep, and state the substitution/equivalence distinction explicitly

claims.basis: true of the seven logged reproduction discrepancies, each verified. But the per-segment scores were never persisted, so the headline metrics are not independently re-derivable from artifacts - an open auditability gap
claims.action: record the score-persistence gap as an unresolved item

claims.claim: BrushlessMotor 58.98 is benchmark discrimination on the released cohort, not mechanical-fault sensitivity
claims.basis: the confound disclosure is carried in the report, the config, and every one of the 42 primary_auc.csv rows via scientific_limitation_id

claims.claim: the upstream best-checkpoint aliasing means the final epoch was scored
claims.basis: PyTorch aliasing verified empirically on a toy model: state_dict returns live references, later optimizer steps mutate them, BatchNorm running stats included. The reproduction deliberately performs no restore

claims.claim: the project's data path, windowing, feature construction, model and scoring are consistent with the published work
claims.basis: Protocol A uses per-window standardised raw multi-sensor input, not the Phase-3.1 98-feature representation. 'feature construction' implies the engineered feature pipeline was validated; it was not

ledger.gap: no test pins the number of Protocol-A looks; a third undisclosed Protocol-A entry would not fail the suite

next_gate_recommendation.rationale: the overlap is now quantified and shown to be asymmetric on the normal class, which makes the bias mechanism concrete while leaving its magnitude the largest unresolved scientific question in the project
